newsitem.title: GERMANY: Contact group concerned at Bosnian Serb crisis.
newsitem.headline: Contact group concerned at Bosnian Serb crisis.

text.p: The five-nation Contact Group has expressed "serious concern" over a political crisis in the Bosnian Serb republic and called for its government and institutions to be respected, Germany said on Thursday.

"The recent developments have direct effects on the implementation of the peace agreement and on the prospects for more democracy throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina," the group said in a statement released in by the foreign ministry Bonn.
Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic is engaged in a bitter power struggle with government hardliners allied to indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.

Bonn said senior Contact Group officials had met in The Hague on Wednesday and agreed on a statement on the situation in the Bosnian Serb republic. The contact group is made up of the United States, Russia, Britain, France and Germany.
"At its meeting on July 2 in The Hague, the Contact Group expressed its serious concern about the current political crisis in the Republika Srpska," the statement said.
"The legal government bodies and institutions of the Republika Srpksa must be respected. Radovan Karadzic, on the other hand, is indicted on war crimes and should be extradited."
In a comment likely to be interpreted as tacit support for Plavsic, the statement noted: "At present, he (Karadzic) is excluded with his own consent from political activity and influence."
The statement also said the international community would not tolerate the use of violence and urged all parties to resolve their differences in accordance with the constitution.
"Otherwise, the Republika Srpska risks an even greater loss of international sympathy and support," the group cautioned.
It added that the Serbian government in Belgrade also bore responsibility for supporting the peace process.
